target.title: fix(plugins): recurring plugin-scheduled jobs silently deleted after first post-boot agent turn
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins that create recurring session turns through `api.session.workflow.scheduleSessionTurn` could lose those persistent cron jobs after normal post-boot plugin-registry churn. The row disappeared silently and the schedule did not fire again until a later restart re-seeded it.

## Root Cause

The original report correctly identified registry churn as the trigger, but the revised caller guard duplicated the compatibility lookup already performed by `ensureStandaloneRuntimePluginRegistryLoaded`, so both checks hit or missed together.

Gateway registries are also pinned for channel, HTTP, and session-extension surfaces. An agent-scoped active-registry replacement therefore does not directly retire the cron-owning Gateway registry.

The deletion path was cross-owner cleanup:

- Dynamic scheduled turns are indexed process-wide and carry their `ownerRegistry`.
- A different registry retiring for the same plugin ID could sweep those records without checking ownership.
- The cleanup callback then called `cron.remove()` on a job owned by the still-live pinned Gateway registry.
- Runtime scheduling, unscheduling, and attachment APIs also required exact active-registry identity even though their API lifecycle declares them late-callable. A pinned live registry therefore became unusable as soon as another registry became active.

## Fix

- Scope dynamic scheduler cleanup to the registry that is actually retiring.
- Preserve broad cleanup for non-registry lifecycle call sites.
- Let runtime workflow APIs operate while their registry is activated, loaded, guarded, and unretired, including when it remains live through a pinned surface.
- Continue rejecting calls before activation and after retirement.
- Leave loader compatibility, workspace, configuration, plugin-scope, and runtime-mode isolation unchanged.

## Evidence

Maintainer rewrite at `a83a53d4a16a6d0144948f3628bab144307886f5`:

- Owner-boundary regression proves retiring registry cleanup removes its own dynamic job while preserving the same-plugin job owned by another live registry, then removes that preserved job when its true owner retires.
- Pinned-registry contract proves schedule and unschedule remain live through active-registry churn, then fail closed after all pins release and the owner retires.
- Equivalent attachment lifecycle contract covers the other late-callable API using the same guard.
- `pnpm test src/plugins/contracts/scheduled-turns.contract.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/session-attachments.contract.test.ts src/plugins/runtime.test.ts`: 58 passed on Blacksmith Testbox.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed core, core-test, extension, and extension-test typechecks; formatting; lint; plugin boundaries; import-cycle checks; and all selected guards.
- Fresh branch autoreview: clean, patch correct 0.89.
- The final hosted PR diff is five files, +143/-13. The superseded caller-guard source and mock-only tests are absent from the effective diff.

The focused suite initially caught an over-broad activation-in-progress guard; the final implementation now distinguishes an activated live registry from one still loading.

## Docs and Release Notes

No docs change is required; existing plugin SDK contracts already describe recurring scheduling and late-callable runtime APIs. `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned.

Thanks to @danseerintel for the production report, diagnosis, and original reproduction work. Contributor credit is preserved in the maintainer rewrite.

---

AI-assisted PR. The final maintainer rewrite was source-reviewed against registry owners, cleanup callers, Gateway pins, scheduled-turn contracts, adjacent attachment contracts, and current `main`, then verified on Blacksmith Testbox.
